issue.title: sase-core provider_priority concurrency test fails with LockTimeout when TMPDIR/CARGO_TARGET_DIR are redirected onto /home
issue.description:
FOUND BY the sase-yf.3 land agent while triaging the `PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP:` note left on
phase bead sase-yf.3.1 (note #1, 2026-09-08 14:46 EDT). NOT caused by epic sase-yf /
sase-yf.3: that epic only touches the SASE-repo ACE prompt model-alias completion menu
and its Python/TUI tests; it changes nothing in `crates/sase_core/src/provider_priority.rs`.

Reported by sase-yf.3.1: running the sase-core repository-wide `just check` with TMPDIR
and CARGO_TARGET_DIR redirected onto /home (the workaround this host needs because the
default shared Cargo target on /mnt/poseidon is out of space) fails
`provider_priority::tests::concurrent_priority_changes_and_auto_disables_are_serialized`
with `ProviderPriorityError::LockTimeout`, and an exact rerun of the same node on the same
tree failed identically. That is why this is filed as a ci failure rather than a flake.

Not independently reproduced by the land agent: rebuilding sase-core test binaries under a
redirected CARGO_TARGET_DIR is a multi-minute cold compile, and the land agent's remaining
budget went to recovering this epic's stranded phase-2 work. Treat the failure observation
as sase-yf.3.1's, and the code reading below as the land agent's.

Code reading at sase-core f79d58b (v0.32.50),
`crates/sase_core/src/provider_priority.rs:1461`: the test spawns 8 threads (4
`set_provider_priority_relative`, 4 `set_provider_disable_relative`) released together by a
`Barrier::new(9)`, and every thread `.unwrap()`s its result. All 8 contend for the single
exclusive provider-disable file lock, whose acquisition wait is deliberately bounded — the
sibling test `lock_wait_is_bounded` (same file, immediately above) asserts a blocked
`get_provider_priority` returns `Err(ProviderPriorityError::LockTimeout)` in under 2s. So
any thread that loses the lock race for longer than that bound panics through `.unwrap()`.
A slow or contended filesystem for the `tempdir()` home — exactly what redirecting TMPDIR
onto a busy /home does — is a plausible mechanism, but the bound, the actual wait
distribution, and the correct repair (raise the bound for writers, retry, or serialize the
test) are all unproven. Diagnose before choosing a fix; do not simply delete the assertion
or the concurrency coverage.

Triage: searched all task statuses for `provider_priority`, `LockTimeout`, and
`concurrent_priority_changes`; swept every task bead created in the last week; reviewed the
31 in-progress epic plans. sase-y8 / sase-x1 / sase-x2 / sase-wv / sase-y7 are SASE-repo
pytest parallel-lane flakes in unrelated subsystems, not this Rust node. sase-xv
(`sase-core just check omits the selected Python shared-library path`) and sase-xw (stale
artifact reuse in the shared /mnt/poseidon Cargo target) are adjacent sase-core build-lane
defects but neither is this lock-timeout failure. sase-xf (`Temporary provider priority in
Provider Routing`) is the closed epic that introduced this module, not an active causal
owner. No duplicate and no causally responsible active epic, so a new task.

task_type_fields.sha: sase-core master on 2026-09-08 (v0.32.48-era); code unchanged at f79d58b v0.32.50
task_type_fields.why_not_flake:
sase-yf.3.1 reported that it failed on the full sase-core `just check` and then failed
again on an exact rerun of the same node on the same unchanged tree, so no pass was ever
observed on that tree — the `flake` type explicitly requires a passing rerun. The failure
is environment-conditional (it needs TMPDIR/CARGO_TARGET_DIR redirected onto /home, which
this host currently requires because /mnt/poseidon is 100% full), but within that
environment it reproduced deterministically. If a later reporter does observe a pass on an
unchanged tree under the same conditions, add that as corroborating evidence rather than
refiling as a flake.

payload.description: Adjacent sase-core just check lane defect discovered by an agent running the repository-wide core check; fixes touch the same core verification entry point

Both are sase-core verification defects tied to the shared /mnt/poseidon Cargo target: sase-xw is stale artifact reuse from it, and this failure only appears under the CARGO_TARGET_DIR redirection used to work around it
